title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is axiomatising the 'déploiement' (unfolding) of a stratified space Σ with conical neighbourhoods. The unfolding is a contravariant system d ↦ Σ*(d), indexed by finite non-empty totally ordered sets d and their inclusions, so in effect a semi-simplicial space. Σ*(0) is Σ cut open along its strata into a 'manifold with boundary'. Σ*(1) parametrises pairs (point of a lower stratum, direction in its link). Σ*(d) parametrises flags of length d+1.

The two inclusions {0},{1} ⊂ {0,1} give two maps Σ*(1) → Σ*(0):
- 'source' sends a link point to its base point in the deeper stratum.
- 'but' / 'bord' sends it to the boundary of the unfolded space.

The previous page imposed local transversality: near each point, the Σ*(d) are transversal intersections of 'bordant' subspaces of Σ*(0). This page adds global 'conditions de circonstance':

(c) The source map Σ*(1) → Σ*(0) is proper and fibrant, i.e. a locally trivial fibre bundle ('condition d'isotrivialité'). Consequently, for any inclusion d ⊂ d' with d an initial segment of d', the map Σ*(d') → Σ*(d) is fibrant. These are the tube or link bundles over unfolded deeper strata.

(d) 'Non-singular condition': Σ*(0) is a manifold with boundary and the 'bord' map Σ*(1) → Σ*(0) has image the boundary. Grothendieck argues the same then holds for all Σ*(d), since a bordant subspace of a manifold with boundary is again one. He is unsure whether this follows ('??') or should be imposed: 'ou exigera que les Σ*(d) soient des variétés à bord'. This is a 'quasi-singular-smooth' condition.

(e) The source map has fibres that are manifolds with boundary (the unfolded links). The induced fibration of their boundaries is the image of Σ*(2) under the face map attached to {0,2} ⊂ {0,1,2}. In words: the boundary of the link of S0 in S2 is fibred through the intermediate strata S1 — links of links.

The marginal note says that in all cases the image of the bord map is a (locally) bordant part. It asks whether the description of the boundary of Σ*(d') via the higher Σ*'s is a consequence of (d), and flags this as delicate in view of what was seen for Σ*({0,2}).

The next page makes it precise:
- Points of Σ*(1) over x under 'but' correspond bijectively to local boundary-hypersurface germs at x.
- Points of Σ*(d) over x correspond to d-element subsets of these germs.

This is exactly the corner structure of a manifold with corners whose boundary hypersurfaces are separated (normalised). In modern terms the page is axiomatising a resolution of a Thom–Mather / conelike stratified space into a manifold with corners carrying an iterated fibration structure, packaged semi-simplicially.
errors: 'Variété à bord' must really mean manifold with corners: once the depth is ≥2, Σ*(0) has corners. The 'bord' map Σ*(1) → Σ*(0) is then not injective over corner points (its fibre is the set of local hypersurface germs, as the next page b1 says). So the hookrightarrow arrow and the phrase 'a comme image son bord' are only correct as statements about images.

The claim that a bordant subspace of a manifold with boundary is a manifold with boundary is not justified on the page. Grothendieck himself hesitates ('??') and offers to impose it as an axiom instead.
The deduction of fibrancy of Σ*(d') → Σ*(d) for initial segments d from condition (c) alone is asserted, not proved. It plausibly needs the transversality conditions of the preceding page as well.
The marginal note itself flags a gap: the description of the boundary of the fibres (condition e) may not follow from (d), and the case Σ*({0,2}) is 'délicat'.

ideas.what: Unfolding (déploiement) of a stratified space into a system of manifolds with boundary/corners, indexed by finite totally ordered sets (flags of strata), with face maps 'source' and 'but/bord'
ideas.modern_name: Resolution of a Thom–Mather stratified space into a manifold with corners; 'unzipping' of conically smooth stratified spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Verona (resolution of Thom–Mather spaces, 1984); Brasselet–Hector–Saralegi (dépliage, 1990s); Albin–Leichtnam–Mazzeo–Piazza (2012); Ayala–Francis–Tanaka (2017)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5–6 on tame topology / dévissage of stratified structures, in sketch form only

ideas.what: Source maps proper and locally trivial; Σ*(d') → Σ*(d) fibrant for initial-segment inclusions
ideas.modern_name: Iterated fibration structure on boundary hypersurfaces (boundary fibration / iterated edge structure)

ideas.what: Boundary of the unfolded link fibres equals the image of Σ*(2) under the {0,2} ⊂ {0,1,2} face (links of links)
ideas.modern_name: Compatibility of iterated fibrations at corners (boundary of link bundle fibred through intermediate strata)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mather control data compatibility; ALMP iterated fibration compatibility

ideas.what: Σ*(d) over x ↔ d-element sets of local boundary hypersurface germs (next page); the 'bord' map as normalisation of the boundary
ideas.modern_name: Corner functor C_k(X) / k-fold boundary ∂^k X of a manifold with corners; ⟨n⟩-manifold faces

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up an axiomatic semi-simplicial 'déploiement' Σ* with explicit global axioms: properness and isotriviality of source maps, a manifold-with-boundary condition, and boundary of link fibres given by the {0,2}-face of Σ*(2). He leaves open which axioms are consequences of the others. Neither the axiomatic packaging as a functor on finite ordinals (with both source and boundary face maps) nor the redundancy question appears to have been settled in this form.
missed.quote: il faudrait voir si le bord de Σ*(d') ... n'est pas une conséquence de (d) ... d'être délicat !
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Modern equivalences between conically smooth stratified spaces and manifolds with corners plus iterated fibrations (Ayala–Francis–Tanaka; ALMP) use different, often heavier axioms. A minimal semi-simplicial axiomatisation would interface directly with exit-path / ∞-categorical descriptions of stratified spaces.

missed.claim: The Σ* system is simultaneously a semi-simplicial space of flags (closely related to exit-path / link data) and the corner system of a manifold with corners. This links the combinatorial exit-path picture to the geometric resolution picture in one object, years before either literature existed.
missed.quote: si d ⊂ d' ... d soit segment initial de d', alors Σ*(d') → Σ*(d) est fibrante
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is the bridge exploited much later in the stratified homotopy hypothesis and in unzipping constructions. It is historically noteworthy that Grothendieck formulated it in 1981–82.

deep.surprise_reason: The general programme of dévissage/déploiement is announced in Esquisse d'un programme. But the explicit axioms here are unpublished detail anticipating later resolution and iterated-fibration theory: proper isotrivial source maps, fibrancy for initial segments, and link boundaries via the {0,2}-face. The page is a sketch with open questions, not a finished result.
transcription_corrections: 'condition d'instrinsidité' should likely read 'condition d'isotrivialité' (local triviality, matching 'fibrante').
'telle impliquée que' is likely 'Cela implique que'.

In (e) the reading is likely: 'Le morphisme Σ*(1) →source Σ*(0) (propre et fibrant, cf (c)) est de plus à fibres des variétés à bord, et la fibration des bords est l'image de Σ*(2) par Σ*(2) → Σ*(1) associé à {0,2} ↪ {0,1,2}'.
In (d), 'une sous-espace bordant' should be 'un sous-espace bordant'.
Margin: 'partie bordante' is probably 'partie localement bordante'.
'(condition quasi-singulière-lisse)' has 'des variétés' inserted as a superscript correction.
